Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q2 FY2025 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There may be a brief pause while we poll for questions. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q2 FY2025 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, CTO; Morgan Patel, Chief Revenue Officer; Casey Nguyen, Chief Product Officer; and Riley Thompson, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q2 FY2025. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on seven key areas: expansion revenue from existing customers, trends in average contract value or ACV, gross margin performance, operating margin expansion, our LTV to CAC ratio, the Rule of 40 metric, and the key assumptions underlying our guidance. These areas highlight our disciplined growth and path to profitability in the enterprise workflow automation market.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss the financials in more detail, including deep dives into these focus areas.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $258 million, representing a 32% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82.4%, and operating income was $72.8 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first half of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $1.85 billion to $1.90 billion.

Let me now walk through each of our seven key focus areas in detail, as they underscore the strength of our SaaS model.

Starting with expansion revenue from existing customers, which is central to our land-and-expand strategy. In Q2, expansion revenue reached $28.7 million, up 52% year-over-year and 18% sequentially. This represented 32% of our total revenue of $89.2 million—our highest mix to date—and propelled our dollar-based net revenue retention, or NRR, to 118%, exceeding our long-term target of over 110%.

Breaking it down, upsells accounted for 45% at $12.9 million, driven by upgrades from our core Orchestrator module for automated CI/CD pipelines to the Enterprise tier with predictive scaling and zero-downtime deployments. Our new AI-Optimized Workflows add-on, powered by generative AI similar to GitHub Copilot or Snowflake's Cortex, saw 240 customers upgrade, adding an average $145,000 in incremental ARR per deal. This reflects enterprise priorities around AI-driven efficiency amid talent shortages, yielding 125% NRR on these upsells.

Cross-sells made up 35% or $10 million, with attach rates rising to 28% from 22% a year ago for modules like Security Sentinel and Data Governance—much like ServiceNow's expansion from IT service management. Mid-market accounts showed land-and-expand cycles under six months via in-app trial prompts; for instance, a regional healthcare provider expanded from Orchestrator to full-stack observability and compliance, tripling their spend.

Usage-based expansion contributed 20% or $5.8 million, as seat expansions and API volumes grew 41% year-over-year on compute-intensive AI workloads, especially real-time fraud detection in fintechs with 15-20% overages.

By region, North America drove 68% or $19.5 million with 122% NRR from Fortune 500 bank renewals. EMEA rose 67% year-over-year to $5.2 million via GDPR-compliant AI in the UK and Germany. APAC surged 89% to $3.1 million in Japan and Australia amid cloud migrations, targeting the $50 billion regional DevOps TAM.

Our customer success team of 180 CSMs now uses an Expansion Playbook with predictive analytics to spot opportunities 90 days pre-renewal, lifting expansion-only cohort NRR to 135%. We expect Q3 expansion at $32-35 million with our upcoming Federated Learning module for multi-cloud orchestration. This engineered expansion grew remaining performance obligations 40% year-over-year to $1.2 billion, supporting 35-40% FY25 growth.

Next, turning to average contract value, or ACV, a leading indicator of our upmarket shift. In Q2, dollar-based ACV hit $48,200, up 18% year-over-year and 5% sequentially—our sixth straight quarter of double-digit growth, outpacing 32% overall ARR growth.

By segment, enterprise ACV over $100k ARR soared 25% to $285,000 on multi-million deals, including expansions with Fortune 100 financial firms adding AI Agent Builder to RPA. Mid-market ACV rose 15% to $65,400 via bundled pricing with predictive analytics. SMB ACV grew 8% to $12,800, balancing volume with upmarket paths.

This ties to 128% NRR, with expansion at 42% of ARR bookings. Our Workflow Everywhere initiative integrates with AWS Bedrock and Snowflake Cortex, enabling 30% cohort ACV uplift in 12 months via autonomous process orchestration cutting manual work by 70%. We applied 5-7% renewal pricing uplifts on high-usage tiers without churn impact.

Regionally, North America led with 22% growth to $52,100 on BFSI and healthcare wins. EMEA rose 16% to $44,500 in DACH with GDPR AI. APAC jumped 28% to $39,800 in Japan/ANZ supply chains via SAP S/4HANA integrations. LatAm grew 10% to $28,200, bolstered by Accenture partnerships.

Enterprise now 55% of bookings from 42%, with sales cycles at 4.5 months and 3-5x ROI proofs. As IT budgets flatten per Gartner, we position against legacy like Automation Anywhere with 2-3x faster value. We see Q3 ACV at 16-20% growth on a $450 million enterprise pipeline, targeting $55,000+ by FY25 end.

Now, on gross margins, which highlight our scalability. For Q2, GAAP gross margin was 82.5%, up 130 basis points sequentially from Q1 and 270 basis points year-over-year. Non-GAAP, excluding $4.2 million in stock-based comp and payroll taxes in COGS, it reached 84.1%—our best in two years. Full-year prior was 81.9% GAAP, up 340 basis points.

Drivers included a mix shift to higher-margin enterprise subscriptions like WorkflowForge and ForgeAI analytics, now 62% of ARR from 48%, adding 90 basis points QoQ via 120-150% ACV premiums with similar costs.

COGS fell to 17.5% from 18.8% YoY on $18 million annualized multi-cloud savings, migrating 35% workloads to Google Cloud and Azure with spot instances—dropping hosting per core user 14% to $1.42 amid 28% ARR growth to $428 million and 118% NRR.

Headwinds: personnel COGS up 5% QoQ for 1,450 new logos and 92% retention, especially EMEA support doubling to 85 for 42% ARR growth. GDPR/EU AI Act compliance added 20 basis points, APAC data localization 8%. Software amortization rose to $11.2 million on $250 million R&D for agentic AI with Anthropic/OpenAI—cash gross margin at 87%.

North America at 85.2% on self-serve; EMEA to 80.4% via ForgeOps reducing deployments 40%; APAC at 75.8%, targeting 80%+ with Alibaba. We expect Q3 at 82.7-83.2%, expanding to 84%+ on AI mix to 70%, 15-20% unit cost cuts via Kubernetes, and buybacks.

Shifting to operating margin, we delivered 28.2% non-GAAP, up 320 basis points YoY from 25.0% and 110 basis points sequentially—seventh straight quarter of expansion toward 30%+ long-term.

Revenue grew 32% to $258 million on 122% NRR—28% ARR expansion to $1.05 billion in CloudForge Platform with Salesforce/Microsoft integrations. Recurring subs at 92% mix.

Gross margins at 82.4%, up 50 basis points YoY on AWS/Azure optimizations and Snowflake-inspired data lake cutting costs 22% at 99.99% uptime.

OpEx grew 22% YoY, 14 points slower than revenue, hitting Rule of 60 at 60.2.

Sales/marketing at 32% of revenue from 36%, payback to 14 months via ABM yielding 45% win rates on $1M+ deals; enterprise ACV $450k up 15% on AI Copilot upsells at 25%.

R&D steady at 18%, ROI from low-code and zero-trust boosting PLG 40%, ahead of Monday.com in APIs.

G&A to 5.8% from 6.5% via automation; revenue per employee $370k at 2,800 FTEs.

North America 29% margin at 68% revenue; EMEA 26% on 45% growth; APAC breakeven from loss. Tiered AI pricing up effective rates 8%, net churn 3.2%. Q3 at 28.5-29.0%, FY at 27.5%+ on AI and $15M savings.

On LTV/CAC ratio, it reached 4.2x in Q2, up from 3.8x prior quarter and 28% YoY from 3.3x—above 3x benchmark per Bessemer.

LTV: cohort ARPU $142 x 118% NRR x 82% margin / 4.2% churn = $4,680. CAC $1,115, down 12% QoQ, payback 14 months.

PLG via freemium Collaborate with Genie AI copilot (92% accuracy, 25% activation lift); self-serve 62% new ARR from 48%, 18% free-to-paid.

North America 4.5x on 70% mid-market share; EMEA 4.0x up from 3.2x with Siemens/SAP; APAC 3.7x on Japan/India growth; LATAM 3.1x improving.

Validates land-and-expand like Zoom; outperforms Salesforce 3.5x, Monday.com 3.9x. $25M FY25 AI marketing for 20% CAC cut, 120% NRR.

For Rule of 40—ARR growth + FCF margin—we scored 62% FY24, up from 55%, best ever above 40 for four years.

ARR $528M, 37% YoY on $112M new ACV (28% up), 128% NRR. North America 42%, EMEA 55%, APAC 62%. FCF $132M, 25% margin up 500 bps on 82% gross, 28% op margin.

Trends: FY22 48%, FY23 55%, FY24 62%. PLG 18% conversions, 75% $1M+ wins, 4.2% churn. FY25 60-65% with 30-35% growth, 28-30% FCF.

Finally, key assumptions for FY25 guidance: $1.85-1.90B revenue (18-22% growth midpoint), 28-30% op margin, $2.45-2.55 non-GAAP EPS—resilient SaaS amid 21% cloud CAGR per Gartner.

Revenue: NRR 112-116% like Q4 114%, 25% cohort expansion top 2,000, 5-7% Enterprise pricing. New ACV $450k up from $420k, AI suite 35% bookings, 10-15% H1 velocity via Snowflake/Databricks. 65% new ARR existing, <5% Enterprise churn, 8% SMB.

Margins: 82-83% gross on AWS Graviton/15% COGS cut; SMG&A 45% from 48%, 12% CAC payback to 14 months, 28% pipeline conversion; R&D 18% on genAI, zero-ETL, edge APAC. $50M SBC savings, 5% headcount to 2,800 sales-focused.

Regions: US 55% 20% growth FedRAMP 2x ACV; EMEA 25% 25% on GDPR AI; APAC 20% 30% despite forex (USD/Asia 105). Enterprise 80%, SMB 28%; $150M usage analytics.

Macro: 2-2.5% US GDP, Fed cuts H2, 12% enterprise software 2025 per IDC. Share gains vs Oracle HCM, AI regs tailwinds.

Risks: high rates/FX/NRR <110%; stress-tested 10% churn limits to 15% growth. Confident in 95%+ retention, $28B TAM 15% CAGR.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Kim for a technology update.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers.

And now Casey Nguyen will provide an update on the product roadmap.

Casey Nguyen:
Thank you, Taylor. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the launch of Workflow Everywhere 2.0. This new feature significantly improves workflow efficiency by up to 70% through autonomous AI orchestration. We are seeing strong adoption of this feature which aligns with our product strategy.

Riley Thompson:
Thank you, Casey. This quarter our focus was on increasing our brand awareness and lead generation through targeted digital campaigns and strategic partnerships. We saw a 25% increase in website traffic and a 35% increase in qualified leads, demonstrating the effectiveness of our marketing initiatives.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. To ask a question, press star one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, how it compares to your initial expectations, and what's the competitive landscape like?

Morgan Patel:
Thanks, Ben. ForgeAI has been a game-changer, contributing over 25% of new bookings and driving 15% of our overall revenue growth this quarter through seamless upsells. Attach rates are at 42% across our enterprise base, exceeding our 30% target. This outperforms initial expectations by 20% in adoption speed, thanks to quick ROI proofs. Competitively, our native cloud-native integrations give us an edge over legacy players like UiPath, where we've won back 15% market share in AI workflow automation.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, what are your key target markets, and what are your expected ROI from these investments?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, Lisa. We're accelerating APAC expansion with new data centers in Tokyo and Singapore, targeting Japan, India, and ANZ as key markets—$15 billion TAM in cloud analytics. Investments include localized teams and partnerships like SoftBank. We expect 3x ROI within two years, building on 62% YoY growth there.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan.

Mike Rodriguez:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, what are your strategies to improve customer retention, and what's the impact of pricing changes on churn?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Mike. Churn remains low at 4.2% gross dollar, best-in-class, managed via proactive AI health scoring in customer success. NRR trended up to 118% from 114%, with expansions offsetting any macro softness. Retention strategies include our Expansion Playbook and CSMs flagging risks early, hitting 95%+ renewals. Pricing changes—5-7% on high-usage—have been neutral to positive on churn, boosting effective pricing without pressure.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Key assumptions: Outline key assumptions underlying guidance.
LTV/CAC ratio: Report the Lifetime Value to Customer Acquisition Cost ratio.
Operating margin: Report operating margin and explain drivers.
Gross margin: Report gross margin and explain changes from prior periods.
Average contract value (ACV): Report and explain trends in average contract value.
Rule of 40: Report the Rule of 40 metric (Revenue Growth + Profit Margin).
Expansion revenue: Detail revenue growth from existing customers.

aspect_summary.Key assumptions: FY25 guidance assumes $1.85-1.90B revenue (18-22% growth), NRR 112-116%, 25% cohort expansion in top 2,000 customers, 5-7% enterprise pricing, new ACV $450k, AI suite 35% of bookings, 65% new ARR from existing customers, <5% enterprise churn, 8% SMB churn; gross margins 82-83% on COGS cuts; OpEx efficiencies; regional growth (US 20%, EMEA 25%, APAC 30%); macro 2-2.5% US GDP, 12% enterprise software growth; risks include high rates/FX/NRR<110%, stress-tested to 15% growth.
aspect_summary.LTV/CAC ratio: Q2 LTV/CAC ratio reached 4.2x, up from 3.8x prior quarter and 3.3x YoY (LTV $4,680 from cohort ARPU $142 x 118% NRR x 82% margin / 4.2% churn; CAC $1,115, down 12% QoQ); regional: North America 4.5x, EMEA 4.0x, APAC 3.7x; targets 20% CAC cut via AI marketing.
aspect_summary.Operating margin: Q2 non-GAAP operating margin 28.2%, up 320bps YoY from 25.0% and 110bps sequentially (7th straight expansion quarter); drivers: 32% revenue growth to $258M, 82.4% gross margin, OpEx growth 22% YoY (14pts slower than revenue; S&M 32%, R&D 18%, G&A 5.8% of revenue); Q3 outlook 28.5-29.0%, FY 27.5%+ on AI efficiencies and $15M savings.
aspect_summary.Gross margin: Q2 GAAP gross margin 82.5%, up 130bps sequentially and 270bps YoY (non-GAAP 84.1%, best in 2 years; prior FY 81.9%); drivers: mix shift to higher-margin enterprise subs (62% ARR, +90bps QoQ), COGS down to 17.5% YoY on $18M multi-cloud savings (hosting costs -14%); headwinds: personnel +5%, compliance costs; Q3 82.7-83.2%, expanding to 84%+ on AI mix and unit cost cuts.
aspect_summary.Average contract value (ACV): Q2 dollar-based ACV $48,200, up 18% YoY and 5% sequentially (6th straight double-digit growth quarter, outpacing 32% ARR growth); trends: enterprise $285k (+25% YoY), mid-market $65,400 (+15%), SMB $12,800 (+8%); driven by upmarket shift (enterprise 55% bookings), AI upsells, pricing uplifts; regional: NA $52,100 (+22%), EMEA $44,500 (+16%), APAC $39,800 (+28%); Q3 16-20% growth to $55k+ by FY25 end.
aspect_summary.Rule of 40: FY24 Rule of 40 (ARR growth + FCF margin) scored 62%, up from 55% (ARR $528M +37% YoY; FCF $132M, 25% margin +500bps); trends: FY22 48%, FY23 55%; regional growth NA 42%, EMEA 55%, APAC 62%; FY25 outlook 60-65% on 30-35% growth and 28-30% FCF margin.
aspect_summary.Expansion revenue: Q2 expansion revenue $28.7M (32% of total revenue), +52% YoY, +18% sequentially, driving 118% NRR; breakdown: upsells 45% ($12.9M, AI workflows), cross-sells 35% ($10M, modules like Security Sentinel), usage 20% ($5.8M, +41% seats/API); regional: NA 68% ($19.5M, 122% NRR), EMEA +67% ($5.2M), APAC +89% ($3.1M); Q3 $32-35M expected; RPO +40% YoY to $1.2B.
